items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: We had Lil Hardin on piano... And I was on the bass.

ctx.x: They fired Jimmy Polar. Oh yeah. I remember that. You see, I'll give you the lineup of the band we left fairly well with. We had, uh, we think from the piano. We had Lil Hardin on piano. We had Johnny Dotson on Clionet. Joe Oliver on trumpet. Nora Dutre on trombone. Uh, we had, uh, Jimmy Polar on violin. Uh, we had a band. And I was on the bass. Ram was on the drums. Okay. Then, they want to turn this boy loose, give him a note. Didn't give him no notice. Just fired him.

items.title: Lillian Hardin Armstrong Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: Eddie Garland was the one who called the numbers... So, I went over with the band... So, we stayed at this Chinese restaurant

ctx.x: Yeah, Tubby Hall, Tubby Hall, and I see who else was there, oh, and Jimmy Pillai. Oh, on violin. On violin, but they didn't have a piano, they didn't use a piano, so, Mrs. Jones booked them at a Chinese restaurant on the west side. I can't find anybody to tell me the name of that restaurant, of where it was, do you remember?
I don't remember if Ed Garland might have told us, or I've seen Lawrence Dewey, He told me he didn't remember. Well, maybe, maybe Lawrence Dewey might remember.

Well, it was, anyway, it was a Chinese restaurant, because every night they used to give them steaks, and they, the boys used to eat steaks, you know, and they tried out all the piano players around. Mrs. Jones sent them all the men piano players, none of them suited them. So, one night she decided to send me over. So, I went over with the band, and, I asked for the music. So, Eddie Garland was the one who called the numbers, and Lawrence Dewey was the one who used to knock them off, you see. So, I said, where's…
